extracted.intended_audience: neuroscience researchers and clinician-scientists studying ion channel genetics and electrophysiology (KCNQ2/KV7), and molecular neurogeneticists working on epilepsy
extracted.subtask_description: Experimental study characterizing a KCNQ2 (KV7.2) mutation using molecular genetics, heterologous expression in Xenopus oocytes, two-electrode voltage-clamp electrophysiology, molecular modelling and computational neuronal modelling to assess pathogenicity and mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects ethics and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: All patients and their unaffected relatives (or their legal representatives) gave written informed consent to participate in the study. All studies conformed to the standards set by the Declaration of Helsinki, and all procedures were approved by the Ethical Committee of the University of Ulm, Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicit informed consent, conformity with Declaration of Helsinki, and local ethics committee approval when reporting human genetic/clinical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data collection and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: All available family members were interviewed in person or by telephone by an experienced paediatrician (JP), and epilepsy histories were documented and corroborated by other family members, except for I-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect detailed phenotype histories via an experienced clinician and corroborate reports with relatives/records; note any gaps in available clinical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutation detection and control screening
rubrics_metrics.description: In a candidate gene approach the coding regions and exon–intron boundaries of KCNQ2 were PCR amplified ... Patient sequences and those of controls were compared to published sequences for KCNQ2 (GenBank, NM_172107). The heterozygous point mutation (A356G) ... was excluded in 96 normal controls by direct sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplify and sequence coding regions and exon–intron boundaries; compare against reference sequences and a sufficient number of population controls to exclude polymorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-directed mutagenesis and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Site-directed mutagenesis was used to introduce the amino acid exchange E119G in the KCNQ cDNA cloned in the pTLN vector. The insertion of the mutation was verified by automated DNA sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce specific mutations by site-directed mutagenesis and always verify the introduced change (and absence of unintended changes) by automated sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: RNA preparation and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Plasmids were digested with the MluI restriction enzyme to linearize the DNA. Linearized plasmids were in vitro transcribed using the SP6 mMessage mMachine kit ... Purity was checked by gel electrophoresis. Concentration was verified by spectrophotometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linearize plasmid templates, perform in vitro transcription with an established kit, check RNA purity by gel electrophoresis and quantify by spectrophotometry prior to injection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal welfare and approvals for oocyte experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: All procedures met the National Institutes of Health guidelines for the care and use of laboratory animals and were approved by the Regierungspraesidium Tuebingen, Germany. Female Xenopus laevis frogs were anaesthetized with Tricaine (0.1%) and placed on ice to maintain anaesthesia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow national/international animal care guidelines, obtain institutional/regulatory approval, and report anaesthesia and surgical procedures used to obtain oocytes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oocyte preparation and injection protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Oocytes were obtained surgically and immediately treated for 2 h with collagenase (2 mg ml−1) in OR2-solution ... Defolliculated oocytes were stored at 16°C in frog Ringer solution ... Diluted cRNA 10–20 ng was injected into each oocyte within 24 h after preparation. Electrophysiological recordings were performed 3 days after injection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full details of defolliculation, storage solution and temperature, RNA amount injected per oocyte, timing of injections relative to harvest, and post-injection incubation time before recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-microelectrode voltage-clamp recording conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Potassium currents were recorded using standard two-microelectrode voltage clamping, a Turbo TEC01C amplifier and pCLAMP data acquisition ... Recording electrodes were filled with 3 M KCl and had a resistance of 0.3–1 MΩ. Currents were low-pass filtered at 0.3 kHz and sampled at 1 kHz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify amplifier and acquisition systems, electrode fill and resistance, filter and sampling rates; these technical parameters must be reported to assess data quality and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bath and electrode solutions and compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Frog Ringer solution (mM: 115 NaCl, 2.5 KCl, 1.8 CaCl2 and 10 Hepes, pH 7.4) supplemented with 50 μg ml−1 gentamycin. Recording electrodes were filled with 3 M KCl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exact compositions (molarities, pH) of bath and electrode solutions and any antibiotics/agents used during storage/recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voltage-clamp stimulation protocol and tail-current analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Oocytes were clamped to a membrane potential of −80 mV followed by depolarizing 10 mV steps up to +20 mV. Tail currents were recorded at −30 mV and their amplitudes analysed to obtain conductance–voltage plots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe holding potential, step increments and range, and the tail-pulse voltage used to construct conductance–voltage relationships; state how tail-current amplitudes were measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curve fitting and biophysical parameter extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: A Boltzmann equation was fitted to conductance–voltage relationships: I/Imax(V) = 1/(1 + exp[(V − V0.5)/k]), with I/Imax being the initial normalized tail current amplitude, V0.5 the voltage of half-maximal activation and k a slope factor. Time constants of activation and deactivation were obtained by fitting a first order exponential function to the rising phase of the current traces or to the tail current decay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard Boltzmann fits to derive V0.5 and slope k; derive time constants by first-order exponential fits to rising/decaying phases. Report the equations and fitting procedures used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis and reporting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For statistical evaluation two-tailed, unpaired Student's t test was applied (P < 0.05 was considered to be significant). All data are shown as means ± s.e.m. Sample sizes (n) are reported for each condition and P-value significance is annotated with stars (* P<0.05, ** P<0.01, *** P<0.001, **** P<0.0001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the statistical test(s) used, significance threshold, how data are summarized (mean ± s.e.m.), report sample sizes, and adopt a consistent notation for P-value annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalizing and pooling data across experimental batches
rubrics_metrics.description: To pool data from different experiments, amplitudes were normalized to the mean one of KV7.2 or KV7.2/KV7.3 that were injected and recorded in parallel with the mutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining data from multiple batches, normalize to an internal control run in parallel within each batch and state the normalization procedure explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental simulation of heterozygous/physiologic allele ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: To mimic the heterologous condition in a patient carrying one normal and one mutated allele, we also performed coexpressions of E119G with KV7.2 channels ... coexpressions ... in a 1:1, and E119G with KV7.2 and KV7.3 in a 1:1:2 ratio (to mimic the situation in an affected individual carrying 1 mutant KCNQ2, 1 WT KCNQ2 and 2 WT KCNQ3 alleles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design coexpression ratios to model expected stoichiometries in patients (e.g., 1:1 or 1:1:2) and explicitly state the rationale for chosen ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing changes in surface expression vs gating
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate if there could be additional changes in surface expression induced by the mutation, we evaluated absolute current amplitudes at the end of a 2 s depolarization to 0 mV ... Normalized relative amplitudes ranged ... revealing a broad overlap of data points. The pooled data ... exhibited a 34% decrease ... However, a reduction of the current amplitude could not be confirmed for heteromeric coexpressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate analyses of maximal currents (surface expression) and voltage-dependent gating should be performed; report both and consider batch variability and overlap of individual data points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molecular homology modelling with stated assumptions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: We generated a homology model of the S1–S6 domains of KV7.2 based on the X-ray coordinates of the KV1.2 K+ channel crystal structure ... For S1–S3 we generated a peptide chain de novo, assigned α-helical structure, used glycine and proline as potential kinking points ... Force fields used for energy minimizations were GROMOS96 and AMBER. These assumptions represent known limitations of the generated model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting homology models, state the template used, parts modelled de novo, structural assumptions (e.g., α-helices), conformational restraints (gly/pro kink points), energy minimization procedures and force fields, and explicitly declare model limitations and speculative aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational neuronal modelling methodology and parameter fitting
rubrics_metrics.description: We implemented a computer model of a one compartment excitable cell according to Golomb et al. (2006). The M-current is described by a Hodgkin–Huxley type model ... To obtain the parameters α^z, β^z, Vαz, Vβz, Kαz and Kβz, the functions τz and z∞ were simultaneously fitted to the normalized data points ... by minimizing the sum of χ2. All simulations were realized with Matlab V 7.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the cell model and included currents, specify formalism for the current (Hodgkin–Huxley), describe which experimental data were fitted, the fitting target functions, the optimization criterion (sum of χ2), and the software used for simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting pathogenicity: co-segregation, conservation, control absence and functional effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The disease status completely cosegregated with the mutation indicating a full penetrance. Furthermore, the mutation affected a conserved residue and was not found in a large number of normal controls, so that even without considering the functional data, there is substantial evidence to consider the mutation as disease-causing. Our electrophysiological investigations showed ... statistically significant ... changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate pathogenicity using combined lines of evidence: familial co-segregation, evolutionary conservation of residue, absence in population controls, and reproducible functional alterations demonstrated experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of raw traces, fitted curves and derived metrics with sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative raw current traces ... Conductance–voltage curves were constructed by plotting the normalized tail current amplitude ... Lines represent standard Boltzmann functions fitted to the data points. Parameters were as follows: KV7.2 (n=12): V0.5 = −40.7 ± 0.9 mV, k = −8.4 ± 0.3 mV; E119G (n=18): V0.5 = −36.4 ± 0.6 mV, k = −8.2 ± 0.3 mV ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide representative raw traces, fitted curves, numerical fit parameters with standard errors, and sample sizes for each condition to allow independent assessment of effect sizes and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of established software and reporting toolchains
rubrics_metrics.description: Data were analysed using pCLAMP 6 with Microsoft Excel, and Origin 6.1 ... All simulations were realized with Matlab V 7.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the software packages and versions used for acquisition, analysis, plotting and simulations to improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization with prior literature and cautious inference
rubrics_metrics.description: These data are consistent with the experimental findings of this and our previous study ... However, due to the hypothetical nature of our model such specific interactions remain speculative and have to be interpreted with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate findings to previous studies, acknowledge speculative aspects of models, and avoid overstatement; explicitly discuss limitations and alternative explanations.
